0.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧⟦shared:1⟧Read the default BLAST columns in observed alignments and select the six endpoint fields needed for plotting.⟦shared:2⟧⟦shared:3⟧

2.translation: ggchord was originally designed to visualize BLASTn alignments as ribbons between nucleotide sequences. BLAST tables are its default recommended alignment input, and the link fields retain query/subject naming as the plotting tools have expanded.

3.translation: Plotting uses full sequence lengths and precomputed alignments. FASTA supplies backbone lengths and BLAST supplies corresponding intervals. Begin with the default BLAST table, then choose nucleotide or protein coordinates.

4.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ writes tab-separated rows without a header. ⟦shared:1⟧ adds comment lines beginning with ⟦shared:2⟧. Omitting ⟦shared:3⟧ produces human-readable pairwise text. These two commands illustrate nucleotide and protein output.

7.translation: Both tabular formats use these 12 columns, in this order, unless you provide a field list.

10.translation: | 1–2 | ⟦shared:0⟧, ⟦shared:1⟧ | Query and subject sequence IDs. The reader names these roles ⟦shared:2⟧ and ⟦shared:3⟧ and preserves the values |

11.translation: | 3–6 | ⟦shared:0⟧, ⟦shared:1⟧, ⟦shared:2⟧, ⟦shared:3⟧ | Percent identity, alignment columns, mismatches and gap openings |

12.translation: | 7–10 | ⟦shared:0⟧, ⟦shared:1⟧, ⟦shared:2⟧, ⟦shared:3⟧ | One-based inclusive endpoints on each sequence. Descending coordinates preserve alignment direction |

13.translation: | 11–12 | ⟦shared:0⟧, ⟦shared:1⟧ | Expected count and score in bits. Lower E-values and higher bit scores generally indicate stronger hits |

14.translation: Extract the [input bundle](⟦shared:0⟧) and work from the directory containing ⟦shared:1⟧. The example file preserves the first 12 fields of observed HSPs.

17.translation: The reader puts the six plotting fields first in the returned table.

21.translation: A ribbon uses the two sequence IDs and their start and end positions. Keep ⟦shared:0⟧ to colour or filter by identity and ⟦shared:1⟧ to filter by alignment length. For a custom headerless file, pass the actual field order as ⟦shared:3⟧ to ⟦shared:2⟧. For a table already in R, see [link conversion](⟦shared:4⟧).

23.translation: | Objects being compared | Native unit | Alignment input | Next step |

25.translation: | Nucleotide sequences | bp | BLASTn | Supply full FASTA lengths and a link table |

26.translation: | Protein sequences | aa | BLASTp | Declare sequence_unit = "aa" with full protein lengths |

27.translation: | Protein hits on a nucleotide genome | bp | BLASTp + CDS models | Project protein intervals to nucleotide coordinates |

28.translation: One plot uses one coordinate unit. Full sequences supply protein lengths, while HSP endpoints describe only aligned intervals. BLASTx and tBLASTn have endpoints in different units and require a chosen common display domain. Nucleotide strand and protein N→C order have distinct biological meanings.

29.translation: [Draw a native BLASTp protein comparison](⟦shared:0⟧), or continue to [the four plotting modules](⟦shared:1⟧).

30.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧⟦shared:1⟧To locate protein hits on a nucleotide genome, read [CDS coordinate projection](⟦shared:2⟧).

32.translation:
Original EMALE records come from the public gggenomes EMALE dataset.
Only data records are reused; all figures are drawn with ggchord, without copying
upstream figures or plotting code. The input bundle's ⟦shared:0⟧ records URLs,
archive members, line ranges, hashes and selection. Parsing neither reruns
alignments nor establishes biological function.

34.translation: Choose nucleotide or protein coordinates, then check table fields, full lengths and units.
